When Prudhomme was two, his father, a shopkeeper, died. His mother and he relocated to Prudhomme's uncle's house. Prudhomme joined his father's name "Sully" with his surname Prudhomme, becoming Sully-Prudhomme. He was interested in classic literature and mathematics in school. He also considered entering the Dominican order, but decided against it.[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Prudhomme attended the [Lycée Bonaparte](/wiki/Lyc%C3%A9e_Condorcet "Lycée Condorcet"), but eye trouble interrupted his studies. Breast changes like [atypical ductal hyperplasia](/wiki/Atypical_ductal_hyperplasia "Atypical ductal hyperplasia")[[125]](#cite_note-urlUnderstanding_Breast_Changes_–_National_Cancer_Institute-125) found in benign breast conditions such as [fibrocystic breast changes](/wiki/Fibrocystic_breast_changes "Fibrocystic breast changes"), are correlated with an increased breast cancer risk.

[Diabetes](/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes") might also increase the risk of breast cancer.[[126]](#cite_note-pmid23709491-126) Autoimmune diseases such as [lupus erythematosus](/wiki/Lupus_erythematosus "Lupus erythematosus") seem also to increase the risk for the acquisition of breast cancer.[[127]](#cite_note-pmid21237645-127)

Women whose breasts have been exposed to substantial radiation doses before the age of 30 – typically due to repeated chest [fluoroscopies](/wiki/Fluoroscopies "Fluoroscopies") or treatment for [Hodgkin lymphoma](/wiki/Hodgkin_lymphoma "Hodgkin lymphoma") – are at increased risk for developing breast cancer. Radioactive iodine therapy (used to treat thyroid disease) and radiation exposures after age 30 are not associated with breast cancer risk.[[95]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHayesLippman2022"Clinical,_Hormonal,_and_other_Nongenetic_Risk_Factors"-95)

Had she won the [governorship](/wiki/Governor_of_Texas "Governor of Texas"), Hutchison would have been required to vacate her Senate seat by January 2011. If she were to stay in the Senate and not run for governor, she would have been up for re-election to the Senate in 2012. On December 8, 2008, Sharp became the first Democrat to announce his intention to [run for this Senate seat](/wiki/United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas,_2012 "United States Senate election in Texas, 2012"), regardless of Hutchison's decision. Unlike several other candidates for the office, Sharp did not create an exploratory committee but immediately began raising funds and campaigning in 2009.[[16]](#cite_note-16) During his campaign for the Senate, he criticized the governor, Rick Perry, for his comments about [secession](/wiki/Texas_secession_movements "Texas secession movements"). He said in a statement, "During World War II my father was shot in defense of the greatest country on Earth, and I proudly wore the uniform of a United States Army reserve officer. So I'm offended when it becomes acceptable for anybody to talk about Texas leaving the Union. The Kop is the stadium section where Liverpool's most vocal supporters, often referred to as "Kopites", have traditionally gathered.[[80]](#cite_note-80) Historically, the Kop was a terraced stand before it was converted to seating, and it has long been recognized as the heart of Anfield's fan base. His slightly hunched running style allows him to barrel through challenges and protect the ball effectively, and there is a tenacity and doggedness to his carrying that makes him difficult to stop.[[50]](#cite_note-:3-51) Alvarez is used to playing in a two-striker system in a team with an extremely settled style of play.[[50]](#cite_note-:3-51)[[51]](#cite_note-:4-52)

In the 2023–24 season, Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola often used Alvarez as an attacking midfielder in the absence of Kevin De Bruyne. List of countries by GDP (PPP) per capita :: Method :: chunk_0001
The [gross domestic product](/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") (GDP) [per capita](/wiki/Per_capita "Per capita") figures on this page are derived from PPP calculations. Such calculations are prepared by various organizations, including the [IMF](/wiki/IMF "IMF") and the [World Bank](/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank"). As estimates and assumptions have to be made, the results produced by different organizations for the same country are not hard facts and tend to differ, sometimes substantially, so they should be used with caution.

Comparisons of national wealth are frequently made based on *nominal* GDP and [savings](/wiki/Savings "Savings") (not just income), which do not reflect differences in the [cost of living](/wiki/Cost_of_living "Cost of living") in different countries (*see [List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)_per_capita "List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita")*); hence, using a PPP basis is arguably more useful when comparing [generalized](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/generalized "wikt:generalized") differences in [living standards](/wiki/Living_standards "Living standards") between economies because PPP takes into account the relative cost of living and the [inflation rates](/wiki/Inflation_rates "Inflation rates") of the countries, rather than using only [exchange rates](/wiki/Exchange_rates "Exchange rates"), which may distort the real differences in income.

This is why GDP (PPP) per capita is considered one of the indicators of a country's standard of living,[[2]](#cite_note-3)[[3]](#cite_note-4) The relation between [GDP per capita and standard of living](/wiki/Gross_domestic_product#Standard_of_living "Gross domestic product") has been criticized. Alternative measures of standard of living include [list of countries by average wage](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_average_wage "List of countries by average wage"), [median income](/wiki/Median_income "Median income") and [disposable household and per capita income](/wiki/Disposable_household_and_per_capita_income "Disposable household and per capita income").

In 1871, [Harrison Weir](/wiki/Harrison_Weir "Harrison Weir") organised a cat show at the [Crystal Palace](/wiki/The_Crystal_Palace "The Crystal Palace"), London. A pair of Siamese cats were on display that closely resembled modern American Burmese cats in build, thus probably similar to the modern [Tonkinese](/wiki/Tonkinese_cat "Tonkinese cat") breed. The first attempt to deliberately develop the Burmese in the late 19th century in Britain resulted in what were known as chocolate Siamese rather than a breed in their own right; this view persisted for many years, encouraging [crossbreeding](/wiki/Crossbreed "Crossbreed") between Burmese and Siamese in an attempt to more closely conform to the Siamese build. The breed thus slowly died out in Britain.[[1]](#cite_note-BCCUK-1)

[Joseph Cheesman Thompson](/wiki/Joseph_Cheesman_Thompson "Joseph Cheesman Thompson") imported *Wong Mau*, a dark female cat, into [San Francisco](/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), USA, in 1930. Thompson considered the cat's build to be sufficiently different from the Siamese to still have potential as a fully separate breed. *Wong Mau* was bred with *Tai Mau*, a black ("seal") point Siamese, and then bred with her son to produce dark brown kittens that became the foundation of a new, distinctive strain of Burmese. In 1936, the [Cat Fanciers' Association](/wiki/Cat_Fanciers%27_Association "Cat Fanciers' Association") (CFA) granted the breed formal recognition. However, due to continued extensive outcrossing with [Siamese cats](/wiki/Siamese_cat "Siamese cat") to increase the population, the original type was overwhelmed, and the CFA suspended breed recognition a decade later.[[2]](#cite_note-UBCF-2) Attempts by various US breeders to refine the unique Burmese standard persisted, however, and in 1954, the CFA lifted the suspension permanently.[[2]](#cite_note-UBCF-2) In 1958, the United Burmese Cat Fanciers (UBCF) compiled an US judging [standard](/wiki/Breed_standard "Breed standard") that has remained essentially unchanged since its adoption.[[2]](#cite_note-UBCF-2)
